analyses.lens: How the judge verdict and score become pass/fail, plus offline simulation of other verdict rules on calib.raw, run 858c8bf6 (gpt-6-luna-openai) and run 08c34cb4 (nova-lite)

findings.claim: No code rule turns classes, claims or score into pass/fail. The verdict is the judge model's own `verdict` field, passed through unchanged. Classes outside the closed list are dropped, the score is clamped to 0..10, and claims are kept as evidence only. There is no threshold, no severity weighting and no 'any claim = fail' rule in code.
findings.evidence: eval_judge.py:303-325 parse_verdict returns obj['verdict'] as is (docstring: 'a class does not force fail (S255...)'). r2.py:449 calibration pair = (label_verdict, cal_v.verdict). The candidate path at r2.py:609 only overrides to fail on a deterministic hard stop.

findings.claim: The kappa bar is in config. Cohen's kappa must be >= 0.6 on >= 10 pairs with >= 3 pass and >= 3 fail labels. If that fails, a run that is not invalid can only end 'informative', never pass. A run that hits budget_cap is 'invalid' whatever kappa is.
findings.evidence: config.py:59-61 MIN_KAPPA=0.6, MIN_KAPPA_PAIRS=10, MIN_KAPPA_PER_LABEL=3; eval_checks.py:245-276 cohen_kappa and judge_counts; r2.py:479-481; r2.py:_finish ~625-631 (budget_cap gives invalid; not judge_counts gives informative).

findings.claim: The 'any claim = fail' behaviour comes from the judge's prompt, not from code. Rubric rule 2 says an unsupported claim fails 'even when one phrase would fix it'. The fact.embellish definition covers any 'invented description, superlative, rarity or editorial claim' the source does not support. The prompt also says 'A fact class applies only when the OUTPUT states something the SOURCE does not support'. Together these make every evaluative phrase an unsupported claim, and every such claim a fail. That cancels rule 4 (reflection is voice) and the 'report classes also when pass' instruction.
findings.evidence: eval_judge.py:90-92 (rule 2), :95 (rule 4), :156-159 (fact-class rule plus 'report also when pass'); services/quality/taxonomy.yaml:103-112 fact.embellish definition. In 858c8bf6, fact.embellish was reported on 18/18 controls and the verdict was fail on 18/18. Examples on pass-labelled items: 'a long ride', 'a rare experience', 'cool limestone pools'.

findings.claim: The score carries no signal beyond the verdict. The prompt maps 4-6 to 'heavy edit', so a judge that says fail gives 4-6. Scores were 2-6 for both label classes. The score's AUC is 0.531, and no threshold reaches kappa above 0.069.
findings.evidence: eval_judge.py:163-164 score bands. sim2.py: pass-label scores [2,4,4,5,5,5,5,6], fail-label scores [2,2,4,4,5,5,5,5,5,6]. score>=k gives kappa 0.069 (k=3,4), 0.024 (5), 0.027 (6), 0.0 (7). On nova-lite, score>=6 or >=7 gives 0.137 (only t9b-018).

findings.claim: No rule built from the stored claims, classes or score reaches kappa 0.6 on the 18 controls of 858c8bf6 without overfitting. All 511 'fail if any class in S' subsets were tried: 0 reach 0.6 and 3 reach 0.5. The best is fact.misbinding alone at 0.55 (LOO 0.514-0.643). It scores 0.0 on the nova-lite run, and none of its 6 checkable fail hits names the reason the label gives.
findings.evidence: sim3.py. Best subset {fact.misbinding}: LP/JP=6, LP/JF=2, LF/JP=2, LF/JF=8, kappa 0.55. Flipping one item (t9b-004 or t9b-018) gives about 0.667, so one item decides the gate. Its fail hits are 005, 008, 009, 010, 012 and 015. Their label reasons in fixture-1.2.0 are an optional activity shown as included plus a broken FAQ (005), the Mörön 'northernmost capital' claim (008), a heading that contradicts the body (009), dangling references and a missing section (010, 012), and an SEO-title scope breach (015). The judge's misbinding quote on each is a different phrase.

findings.claim: The other candidate rules all fall short of 0.6, and they rest on items near their threshold or on artefacts. 'non-embellish claims >= 3' gives 0.444 (LOO 0.406-0.534), and 9/18 items have 2 or 3 such claims, within one claim of the cut. The weighted rule (embellish 0.25, framing/direction 0.5, slug truncation 0, other 1) gives 0.430 at >= 2.5 or 3. 'Hard-set claims >= 2' gives 0.430. 'All claims >= 8' gives 0.561, but 8 is MAX_CLAIMS, so that rule only means 'the judge hit its claim cap'. Ignoring embellish, or embellish plus framing, plus slug truncation, gives -0.110 because nearly every text keeps another class. Removing the view-cut struct.truncated claims lowers 'non-emb >= 3' to 0.341. On nova-lite no rule passes 0.276.
findings.evidence: sim.py / sim2.py output (confusion matrices in the numbers field). eval_judge.py:57 MAX_CLAIMS=8. Nova-lite gave 1-3 claims per item because its replies were cut at max_tokens.

findings.claim: Even a perfect judge-side rule would need at least 5 of the 8 pass labels judged pass with no false pass to reach 0.6. The current claim stream does not separate the two classes: every pass-labelled text has 3-8 claims and every fail-labelled text has 4-8.
findings.evidence: sim2.py: if the judge passes k true-pass items and no fail item, kappa is 0.526 at k=4 and 0.649 at k=5. Per-item claim counts: pass items 5,6,8,7,7,7,4,3; fail items 8,8,4,8,8,8,8,8,7,5.

findings.claim: The judge reads the OUTPUT cut at 9000 characters with no cut mark. Long blog controls therefore look truncated, and their SEO title, meta and slug go unseen. That produces false struct.truncated claims and hides the fields where label failures sit, such as the 015/016 SEO-title scope breach.
findings.evidence: eval_judge.py:56 OUTPUT_CHARS=9000 and :287 `[:OUTPUT_CHARS]` with no CUT_MARK. Fixture-1.2.0 flattened lengths: t9b-007 9028 (slug cut to 'bhutan-textile-museum-tig'), t9b-011 9994 (view ends 'used acros'; seo_title starts at 9735 and is unseen), t9b-013 9204 (meta starts at 9001). The judge flagged struct.truncated on 007, 011 and 013, and on 016, which is not in the local fixture.

findings.claim: The struct.truncated claims on 017, 018 and 019 point at the real slug 'lake-khovsgol-northern-mongolia-ecological-cultural-crossroa' (60 characters). The labels treat it as light (017 and 018 pass, 019 fails for other reasons). Ignoring slug truncation alone does not move kappa.
findings.evidence: calib.raw judge_claims. The rule 'any non-embellish claim, slug truncation ignored' gives kappa -0.110.

findings.claim: The calibration set contains a test label. t9b-002 is a 'human_label' pass whose reason reads 'ZZ S239 test label'. It is one of the 8 pass labels, and the pipeline verdict on that text was fail.
findings.evidence: docs/eval/aa729/fixture-1.2.0.json t9b-002 label {verdict: pass, source: human_label, reason: 'ZZ S239 test label'}. calib.raw rows for 858c8bf6/08c34cb4 t9b-002 show label_source human_label, label pass. Dropping it: 'raw non-emb >= 3' 0.406, 'clean non-emb >= 2' 0.351. Still under the bar.

findings.claim: Several fail labels rest on structural or coherence defects the judge's closed class list cannot express: dangling references, a missing section, an FAQ answer that does not answer, a duplicated FAQ. struct.leaked_instruction is in the list, but the judge never reported it, although the t9b-012 label cites leaked scaffolding ('This is the section that earns its length').
findings.evidence: eval_judge.py:69-71 JUDGE_CLASSES. Label reasons in fixture-1.2.0 for 005, 007, 009, 010 and 012. 858c8bf6 failure-code counts contain no struct.leaked_instruction. The judge matched the label's reason on 4 of 7 checkable fail items (005 inclusion, 007 invented stock, 009 heading number, 015 SEO-title framing) and missed it on 008, 010 and 012.

findings.claim: The runner keeps paying for writing after calibration has already shown the judge cannot count. With judge_counts false, the run can end at best 'informative', so the writer money buys no attachable verdict. In 858c8bf6 the 18 calibration calls cost about $0.04; the following $2.37 of writer spend could never produce pass.
findings.evidence: r2.py:479-490: after out.judge_counts the loop goes on to the probe/tune/holdout phases with no stop. r2.py _finish: 'not out.judge_counts' gives 'informative'. 858c8bf6: writer 20 calls $2.37, judge 44 calls $0.087 (about $0.002 per call).

findings.claim: The cheap judge-only calibration harness cannot test the judge actually in use. judge_compare.py accepts only Bedrock Converse models served on acc3 and refuses `*-openai` keys, so gpt-6-luna-openai cannot be calibrated there while acc3 is blocked.
findings.evidence: scripts/aa919/judge_compare.py:62-77 refusal(): api_style != converse or provider != bedrock is refused; account_for(acc3) is required.

root_cause_candidates: The judge prompt contradicts itself, not the code. Rubric rule 2 ('an unsupported claim fails even when one phrase would fix it') plus the fact.embellish definition ('invented description ... editorial claim') turn every evaluative adjective into a fail-forcing fact claim, which overrides rule 4 (reflection is voice). That gives 18/18 embellish and 18/18 fail (eval_judge.py:90-95, :156-159; taxonomy.yaml:103-112).

The label task and the judge task differ. The panel labels grade editing effort, and fail labels mostly name structural or coherence breaks plus one or two specific wrong facts. The judge is told to list unsupported claims, its closed class list has no coherence class, and its claims are spread evenly across pass and fail texts. No post-hoc rule over its output separates the two classes; the best of 511 subsets reaches 0.55.

The 9000-character OUTPUT cut with no cut mark (eval_judge.py:56, :287) makes long blogs look truncated and hides the SEO title, meta and slug. This causes struct.truncated false positives on 007, 011 and 013 (and likely 016) and blinds the judge to SEO-field scope failures.

Calibration data noise: t9b-002 is a leftover 'ZZ S239 test label' counted as 1 of 8 pass labels. 004 (pass) and 008 (fail) also hinge on similar Mörön-province wording, which suggests label sensitivity on near-identical claims (INFERRED).
proposed_fixes: Do not ship a code-side verdict rule tuned on these 18 items. The best candidate (fact.misbinding only, kappa 0.55) depends on 1 item to cross 0.6, scores 0.0 on the other judge, and its hits match none of the label reasons.

Fix the prompt so the judge answers the label question. Add a per-claim `severity: light|heavy` field to JUDGE_SCHEMA and state that evaluative adjectives, reflection, comparisons of feel ('long', 'rare', 'richest section') and brief/brand-pack-sourced lines are light (rules 4-5). Compute the verdict in parse_verdict as fail iff any heavy claim or a structure break, keeping the model verdict for audit. Reword rule 2 to apply to checkable trip facts (activity, access, time, view, service, number, name, place binding), matching the source-fidelity policy. The judge_version will change, so recalibration is needed.

Add a closed-list coherence class for the judge (dangling reference, FAQ answer that does not answer, duplicated sentence/section, heading contradicting body), or map it onto fact.self_contradiction / struct.*. 010 and 012 fail only on these, and they partly drive 005, 007 and 009.

Raise OUTPUT_CHARS to at least 12000 (blog outputs reach 9994), or put seo_title/meta/slug before content_text in the judge view, and append CUT_MARK when cutting, so struct.truncated reflects the text and not the view.
Remove t9b-002 ('ZZ S239 test label') from the calibrated golden set, as a fixture bump (7 pass / 10 fail still meets MIN_KAPPA_PER_LABEL).

Add a cost guard to R2: right after calibration (r2.py ~481), if judge_counts is False, stop with a new reason such as 'uncalibrated' before any writer call. Every such run can at best be 'informative'. This would have saved about $2.37 in 858c8bf6 and a similar amount in 08c34cb4.

Before the one approved paid R2 rerun, calibrate the revised judge with judge calls only (18 controls, about $0.04 per pass). Either let judge_compare.py accept the live route model (today it refuses OpenAI and non-acc3 models), or add an R2 calibrate-only mode. Start the paid writer run only once kappa >= 0.6 holds with stable LOO.

analyses.lens: Rubric vs labelling policy: the judge's claims on the 8 PASS-labelled calibration controls in run 858c8bf6 (judge gpt-6-luna-openai, judge version 73e641a99aca, golden set aa729@1.3.0)

findings.claim: The judge prompt that is live now hashes to exactly 73e641a99aca. The verdict rubric is eval_judge.py:84-99 (LABEL_RUBRIC), followed by the judge-only rules at eval_judge.py:155-166. The class definitions come from services/quality/taxonomy.yaml (fact.embellish definition at :110-112, struct.truncated :171, scope.framing :205, scope.persona_promise :219).
findings.evidence: I ran apps/AA-CIS-App/.venv/bin/python on eval_judge.judge_version() and got '73e641a99aca'. The full system prompt is saved at /tmp/claude-1000/-home-nghiep-projects-AA-Ecosys/09351236/scratchpad/aa900-rubric/system_prompt.txt.

findings.claim: I classified all 47 judge claims on the 8 PASS-labelled items. (a) real violation under the labelling policy: 3 firm plus 1 borderline. (b) false positive driven by the rubric wording: 23. (c) false positive from the judge's literal reading even though a rubric line or the SOURCE covers the phrase: 14. (d) the judge was missing input, or saw a cut copy of the input: 6. So 43 of 47 claims (91%) are false positives, and about half come from the rubric text itself.
findings.evidence: Claims are numbered in the order of /tmp/claude-1000/-home-nghiep-projects-AA-Ecosys/09351236/scratchpad/aa900-rubric/pass_claims.txt, and the buckets are in classification.json in the same folder. a=[5,6,23], a?=[42], d=[20,21,22,24,26,33], c=[4,7,8,10,12,15,18,19,27,28,30,34,43,45], b=the other 23. Each claim was checked against the rebuilt judge SOURCE (judge_source_text on fixture 1.3.0, same bytes as R2 uses) and against the frozen output.

findings.claim: The (a) claims, where the label itself is suspect. #5 (t9b-002): the meta description says 'staying with village families along the way', but the source has one homestay night in Ban Long Lao Mai. That is an accommodation promise, which rule 2 (eval_judge.py:90-92) and policy B forbid. #23 (t9b-011): 'generally suits children from around seven upwards' is almost word for word the taxonomy's own positive example for scope.persona_promise (taxonomy.yaml:219,224). #6 (t9b-004): 'Mörön, the capital of Khövsgöl Province and the northernmost aimag in Mongolia' calls the city an aimag. t9b-006 and t9b-018 write it correctly ('Province, the northernmost aimag') and were not flagged, and t9b-008 is labelled FAIL for the same kind of Mörön misbinding. Borderline #42 (t9b-017): 'negotiating a boundary for millennia' is an invented time span, the same kind of claim that the same S259 panel used to FAIL t9b-020 ('a taiga that has barely changed in centuries').
findings.evidence: Source greps: 'homestay' appears only under Ban Long Lao Mai on days 2-3, and the source line is 'Mörön is the capital city of Khövsgöl Province, the northernmost aimag'. The label reasons for t9b-008 and t9b-020 are in fixture-1.3.0.json. 'millenni' has 0 hits in the t9b-017 source.

findings.claim: Bucket (d), 6 claims, comes from the harness. (1) The OUTPUT is cut at OUTPUT_CHARS=9000 (eval_judge.py:56) by a plain slice with no cut mark (eval_judge.py:287). The t9b-011 output is 9994 chars and the t9b-013 output is 9204, so the judge saw text ending mid-field and flagged struct.truncated (#26, #33), although the real outputs end cleanly. (2) The t9b-011 SEED was clipped to its 16000 cap, which dropped the Tsaatan place background. The panel read it in full (panel source 24504 chars, judge source 21027). That background holds 'numbering only a few hundred people', 'Tsagaannuur', 'requires a permit' and 'Tuvan peoples of southern Siberia', which are claims #20, #21, #22 and #24. Across the 18 calibration items, 4 outputs are over 9000 chars (t9b-007, 011, 013, 016) and 3 sources are cut (t9b-011, 015, 016).
findings.evidence: Local rebuild with eval_writers.output_text and eval_judge.judge_source_text/panel_source_text. The text at offset 9000 of t9b-011 is '...used acros|s Central Asia'. The full t9b-013 output ends with a complete meta description and slug.

findings.claim: Bucket (b) is mostly fact.embellish (16 of 23). The class definition reads 'An invented description, superlative, rarity or editorial claim ... that the source does not support' (taxonomy.yaml:110-112). It sits in the fact.* family, so rule 2 applies to it: 'A claim the source does not support is a fact change, so the text fails even when one phrase would fix it' (eval_judge.py:90-92). The judge-only rule 'A fact class applies only when the OUTPUT states something the SOURCE does not support' (eval_judge.py:156-157) makes the source the only test. Rule 4, the only exemption (eval_judge.py:95), covers 'what a place means, why its setting matters' and nothing else. Rankings ('the richest in the sequence', 'one of the most geographically striking'), ordinary adjectives ('a long ride' for 30 km, 'cool limestone pools', 'fertile'), contrasts with other kinds of travel ('not a packaged tour', 'separates ... from a standard active holiday') and figurative lines therefore all read as fact changes, and so as fails.
findings.evidence: Claims #1,2,3,9,11,13,14,16,17,29,35,36,37,38,39,46. None of them is a promise about THIS trip. The labels call these texts light-edit passes.

findings.claim: On superlatives, the rubric is stricter than the product's own policy. The live T9 gate treats superlatives as a style issue: F2_superlatives blocks only on 'more than one stock superlative' and is in STYLE_ONLY_GATES ('one sentence repair, never holds'), quality_gates.py:388-389 and :2214. A single stock superlative is a warning only (quality_gates.py:136, 390). The R2 judge instead turns any editorial superlative into a fail.
findings.evidence: apps/AA-CIS-App/services/acp_content_writing/quality_gates.py:136,388-391,2214.

findings.claim: The rubric does not encode the writer source-fidelity policy. That policy has two parts. Part A (allowed): 'short, well-known background about a place the source names (what it is, era, architecture, setting)'. Part B (forbidden): 'any claim about THIS tour the source does not state: activities/experiences, food & drink, services, transport mode or travel time, clock-times, views/sightings, accommodation features, inclusions'. The rubric keeps B (rule 2 lists 'an activity, access, time, view or service') but has no A at all, and eval_judge.py:156 tests source support only. Background claims are therefore flagged: #16 (comparing the lake with better-known lakes), #42 (millennia), #32 and #40 (place background that is in the SEED, flagged as scope).
findings.evidence: memory/writer-source-fidelity-policy.md (S223, AA-756) compared with eval_judge.py:84-99 and :155-166.

findings.claim: Scope claims (#31, #32, #40, #41) are driven by the fail line 'wrong scope' (eval_judge.py:85-86). They are reinforced by the writer's SCOPE text that the judge reads ('must not promise, name or imply any place ... outside these moments'). The labels say the opposite: t9b-017's label lists 'the FAQ's "flights to Ulaanbaatar" names an itinerary place outside SCOPE' among the wording-only fixes, and t9b-013's label calls the FAQ pair naming Ulaanbaatar/Khatgal a light deletion. The taxonomy definition limits scope.framing to 'title, meta or subtitle (sells a place no day visits)' (taxonomy.yaml:205). Rule 5 (eval_judge.py:96-98) covers only itinerary places the brief asked for.
findings.evidence: Label reasons in fixture-1.3.0.json; the SCOPE section of each rebuilt source; 'Pak Ou' and 'Tuvan peoples of southern Siberia' are in the SEED place background.

findings.claim: The cut slug (#44, #47: 'lake-khovsgol-northern-mongolia-ecological-cultural-crossroa') is a real defect, but our own code produces it: _ascii_slug ends with `folded[:60].rstrip("-")` (acp_content_writing/service.py:908), which cuts mid-word. The t9b-017 label calls 'the slug is cut off' a wording-only fix. The judge reports struct.truncated correctly, but 'broken structure' in the fail line (eval_judge.py:85-86) turns it into a fail, and no rubric line says a slug is light.
findings.evidence: service.py:903-908; the t9b-017 label reason; both outputs end with the 60-char slug.

findings.claim: Bucket (c), 14 claims: the SOURCE or a rubric line already covers the phrase and the judge flagged it anyway. Examples: #10 'not something that can be approximated elsewhere' (the source says 'one of the last of its kind in the world'); #27 the teepee camps / meeting families / reindeer up close (place background, nearly verbatim); #4 and #34 'north' (the source has 'Nam Ou Valley — cycle northbound'); #15 'a rare experience' (the ANGLE BRIEF asks for 'rarity of experience', so rule 5 covers it); #28 pace (the brand style guide says 'Explain the pace clearly' and gives 'Each day balances active disco[very]...'); #43 and #45 loose paraphrases ('long associated' for 'reputed'; 'Mongolia's water' for 'fresh water'), which rule 3 calls light; #18 'the lake comes into view' (the trip goes to a lakeshore camp). The instruction 'Look for the phrase's fact in every SOURCE section first' (eval_judge.py:161-162) exists, and the judge did not follow it.
findings.evidence: ctx.py greps on each rebuilt judge source in the scratchpad folder.

findings.claim: The labels are part of the problem. (1) t9b-002 carries label reason 'ZZ S239 test label' (label_source human_label, grade light). It is the only human_label in the fixture, it is a test stub rather than a judgement, and labels.py:58 (RELABEL_SOURCES = agent_panel only) means a calibration review can never fix it. (2) Five of the 8 pass labels (004, 006, 011, 013, 014) were made in S245, before the S256 rules, and most of them were split votes overruled by the verifier alone. 004 and 011 had 3 of 3 first-pass judges voting fail. The S256 calibration review re-checked only t9_social (label_history 1.1.0→1.2.0 relabelled only t9l-001 and t9l-003), so the t9_blog pass labels were never reviewed under rules 1-5. (3) t9b-011 also contains 'This is the section that earns its length', which is the verbatim positive example of struct.leaked_instruction (taxonomy.yaml:195, severity hard). Its pass label conflicts with rule 2 as well.
findings.evidence: fixture-1.3.0.json labels and label_history; grep shows the leaked sentence appears once in the t9b-011 output.

findings.claim: Changing the rubric alone cannot reach kappa 0.6 with comfort. With the labels unchanged (8 pass / 10 fail), a judge that passes the 5 pass items without a firm (a) claim (006, 013, 014, 017, 018) and fails all 10 fails gets kappa 0.649. If it passes only the 4 clean ones (excluding 017), kappa is 0.526. If it passes 5 but also passes one fail label, kappa is 0.538. If t9b-002 is excluded and 011 and 004 are relabelled fail (5 pass / 12 fail), kappa is 1.0 at perfect agreement, 0.85 when the judge passes 4 of 5 and fails 12 of 12, and 0.717 at 4 of 5 and 11 of 12.
findings.evidence: Cohen's kappa computed locally with the standard formula.

findings.claim: Any loosening of fact.embellish has to keep two fail labels failing. t9b-019 fails on 'difficult to replicate elsewhere in Mongolia', a rarity claim with no source support while TRIP lists Khorgo volcano, plus FAQ defects. t9b-020 fails mainly on 'a taiga that has barely changed in centuries'. A blanket 'embellish = light' rule would flip 020 and possibly 019 to pass. The line needs to separate checkable world claims (rarity or uniqueness, age, duration, ranking stated as fact) from subjective evaluation.
findings.evidence: Label reasons for t9b-019 and t9b-020. In run 858c8bf6, t9b-020's only judge class is fact.embellish.

findings.claim: R2 keeps spending on the writer after a failed calibration. It computes judge_counts after the calibrate phase (r2.py:481) and then enters probe/tune/holdout without stopping (r2.py:490 onward). root_cause_candidates: RUBRIC (largest share, 23/47): fact.embellish is defined as 'invented description, superlative, rarity or editorial claim' (taxonomy.yaml:110-112) and sits in the fact.* family. Rule 2 (eval_judge.py:90-92, 'a claim the source does not support is a fact change, so the text fails even when one phrase would fix it') and eval_judge.py:156-157 then turn every adjective, ranking or contrast into a fail. Rule 4 (eval_judge.py:95) only exempts reflection about what a place means.

RUBRIC: the writer source-fidelity policy A ('well-known background about a place the source names' is allowed) is missing, and 'wrong scope' / 'broken structure' in the fail line (eval_judge.py:85-86) has no light-edit carve-out. So background mentions outside SCOPE (Ulaanbaatar flights, Pak Ou, southern Siberia) and a cut slug fail, while the labels call all of these wording fixes.

HARNESS (6/47): OUTPUT_CHARS=9000 is a silent slice (eval_judge.py:56,287) that makes complete outputs look truncated (t9b-011, t9b-013; 4 of 18 calibration outputs are over 9000 chars). The SEED cap of 16000 (eval_judge.py:63) removed the Tsaatan background the panel read (t9b-011; 3 of 18 sources are cut).

LABELS: t9b-002 is a test stub ('ZZ S239 test label') that cannot be relabelled (labels.py:58). The t9_blog pass labels from S245 were never reviewed under the S256 rules: t9b-011 breaks rule 2 (age 7+) and contains a leaked instruction, t9b-004 has the Mörön misbinding that t9b-008 was failed for, and t9b-017 has 'millennia' against t9b-020's 'centuries'. With the labels as they are, even a correct judge tops out around kappa 0.53-0.65.

JUDGE MODEL (14/47): it ignores the existing 'look in every SOURCE section first' rule and the rules 3 and 5 carve-outs. It flags place-background facts, brief-asked rarity and brand-asked pace, and quotes the wrong span for truncation.
PRODUCT BUG behind 2 claims: _ascii_slug cuts at 60 chars mid-word (acp_content_writing/service.py:908).
COST: R2 runs the paid writer arm even when calibration fails (r2.py:481-490), so an uncalibrated judge burns the cap.
proposed_fixes: Rubric R1, encoding the product's superlative policy (quality_gates.py:388-389, F2_superlatives is STYLE_ONLY, 'one sentence repair, never holds') and fidelity policy B. Add to LABEL_RUBRIC['rules'] and to labels.RUBRIC, which a test keeps equal: 'Subjective evaluation is voice, not a fact: a ranking of the trip's own days or sections, an adjective of degree or feel (long, cool, striking, rich), a contrast with other kinds of travel, figurative wording. Report fact.embellish for it, but it is a wording fix.' Then narrow rule 2 so fact.embellish counts as a fact change only for (i) anything about THIS trip (activity, service, time, view, access, accommodation, inclusion, suitability) the itinerary does not state, or (ii) a checkable claim about the world the SOURCE does not give: rarity or uniqueness ('the only', 'difficult to replicate elsewhere'), an age, duration or era ('for centuries'), or a ranking stated as fact ('the largest lake in Asia'). This keeps fail labels t9b-019 and t9b-020 failing.

Rubric R2, encoding fidelity policy A ('A allowed — short, well-known background about a place the source names (what it is, era, architecture, setting)'). Rule: 'The SEED's "Place background" lines are source. Short background about a place or people the SOURCE names is allowed even outside SCOPE and need not be quoted from the SOURCE; flag it only when it is wrong, contradicts the SOURCE, or becomes a promise about the trip.'

Rubric R3, encoding the S259 label reasons (t9b-017: the FAQ naming a place outside SCOPE and the cut slug are wording-only fixes) and the taxonomy's own scope.framing definition (taxonomy.yaml:205). Rule: 'Scope fails only in the title, SEO title, meta description, subtitle or headings, or when the text sells or promises a place no in-scope day visits. A body or FAQ sentence that names an out-of-scope place for background or logistics (how to fly in, where a people come from) is a light fix.' And: 'A URL slug shortened at its length limit is a light fix; a cut-off sentence in any other field is a fail.'

Rubric R4, separating rule 3 from rule 2 for misbinding: 'A paraphrase that keeps the source's value and subject but words it loosely (drops "fresh", "reputed" → "long associated") is light. A value attached to another subject (a city called a province, 30 species → 30 lakes) is a fact change even when one word fixes it.' This matches the t9b-008 fail label.

Rubric R5, against verdict-by-count: 'Decide the verdict only from the reported phrases that are fact changes under these rules. A text whose phrases are all wording fixes passes (score 7-8), however many there are.' Optionally add a per-claim 'source_quote' field (empty = not found) so the judge has to show where it searched (the S232 lesson). That changes the schema, so it becomes a new judge version.

Harness H1: raise OUTPUT_CHARS to 16000, or clip with CUT_MARK and tell the judge 'an OUTPUT ending in the cut mark was shortened by the grader, not the writer'. Raise the T9 SEED cap or SOURCE_CHARS so that none of the 18 calibration sources is cut (max seed ~19.5k). Judge cost is about 0.002 USD per call, so this adds cents.

Labels L1, a $0 change in a new fixture version and not paid: remove t9b-002 from calibration, or give it a real panel label. Its stub label is a human_label that RELABEL_SOURCES (labels.py:58) blocks from review, so allow an explicit exception for 'ZZ' test labels. Run the S256 calibration review on the 8 t9_blog pass labels under rules 1-5 plus R1-R4. Expected outcome: t9b-011 becomes FAIL heavy (age 7+ promise per taxonomy.yaml:219/224, and leaked instruction per taxonomy.yaml:195). Decide t9b-004 (Mörön misbinding, consistent with t9b-008) and t9b-017 (millennia vs t9b-020). The tech lead approves, as in S256.
Product P1: cut the slug at the last hyphen at or below 60 chars in _ascii_slug (service.py:908). This is a real customer-facing defect, separate from AA-900.

Cost guard C1, before the single paid rerun: make R2 stop after the calibrate phase when judge_counts is false (r2.py:481-490), so a bad judge costs ~0.04 USD instead of 2.4 USD. Alternatively, first run calibration-only on the 18 frozen pairs (judge_compare.py needs to accept the -openai route model, or add an R2 calibrate-only flag). Launch the writer arm only when kappa is 0.6 or higher.

Order, for one paid rerun: L1 labels plus R1-R5 plus H1 (one new judge version) → $0 DRY RUN → calibration-only (~0.04 USD) with kappa ≥ 0.6 → the R2 writer arm under the 2.5 USD cap, with migration 381 effort medium.

root_causes.cause: RC1 (primary): the judge prompt, not the code, turns every evaluative phrase into a fail. Rubric rule 2 says an unsupported claim 'fails even when one phrase would fix it'. The fact.embellish definition covers any 'invented description, superlative, rarity or editorial claim'. The judge-only rule says 'a fact class applies only when the OUTPUT states something the SOURCE does not support'. Read together, any adjective, ranking, contrast or figurative line becomes a fact change and therefore a fail. Rule 4 only exempts reflection about what a place means. The rubric also lacks three things: the writer's 'ALLOWED background about a place the seed names' clause, a light-edit carve-out for background places outside SCOPE, and a light-edit carve-out for a cut slug.

Lý do judge chấm trượt mọi bài nằm ở lời dặn trong prompt, không nằm ở code. Đổi model judge thôi thì không ăn thua: hai model của hai hãng khác nhau cho kết quả giống nhau 17/18 bài.
Tìm ra thêm hai lỗi chặn mà lần chạy trước không thấy: chưa có bài viết mới nào được ghép với bài đối chứng, nên dù judge chấm đúng thì lần chạy cũng không thể đạt. Còn nếu sửa phần ghép mà không sửa luật dừng khẩn thì lần chạy sẽ dừng sớm với kết quả trượt vì lỗi vặt.
